packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-09 - unverified image-only reading
No identification or prior reading of this record was visible in my context.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, overview of first face)
- Two small separate parchment scraps on black ground, ruler at right (scale ~ cm). Left scrap c. 3.5 x 7.5 cm, roughly rectangular, right edge torn ragged. Right scrap c. 5.5 x 8 cm, trapezoidal, wider at bottom, left edge torn with a protruding tag.
- Surface heavily stained/abraded, greyish-brown blotching; at overview scale only faint traces of horizontal lines of script are visible. No colour rubrics or initials visible at this scale.
- Modern pencil notes: left scrap upper left "Stams, StA, Frg. 22-2(?)"; right scrap lower edge "Stams, StA, Frg. 22-1a(?)" (modern shelf labels, not medieval text).
- Orientation appears upright (pencil labels horizontal). Columns cannot be judged from this view.
- Tiles: image-002.jpg and image-003.jpg presumably cover left and right scraps of this face; image-004.jpg is a second overview (other face) with tiles image-005.jpg, image-006.jpg.

TILE image-002.jpg (left scrap, face 1, native resolution)
- Shows the whole left scrap (approx x 45-530, y 135-1165) and the torn left edge of the right scrap at far right.
- Observation: surface is badly abraded and water-stained with vertical grey-brown streaking. In the natural-colour image there are faint dark specks in horizontal rows in the lower half (approx y 560-1030), suggesting lines of writing, but no letter forms resolve. Faint horizontal lines at approx y 770 and y 1015 (more visible in crop-02.jpg) may be drypoint/plummet ruling or the baselines of lost lines; spacing cannot be measured reliably.
- Pencil (modern): "Stams, StA / Frg. 22-2a(?)" at y 300-430.
- Crops: crop-01.jpg (blue channel, autocontrast + equalize, 2x) - amplified the staining only; crop-02.jpg (greyscale, background subtraction of 25-px blur, 2x) - shows faint horizontal banding, no readable letters.
- Transcription: no line can be read. image-002.jpg lines 1-c.10 (lower half of scrap): [illegible] throughout. I could not distinguish ink strokes from stain at native resolution even after enhancement.

TILE image-003.jpg (right scrap, face 1, native resolution)
- Shows the whole right scrap (approx x 120-890, y 30-1190). Pencil (modern) near bottom: "Stams, StA, Frg. 22-1a(?)" at y 980-1030.
- Observation: surface very worn, vertical streaky staining and fibre damage; a loose flap/tag on the left edge (y 560-830). No ink letters visible in natural colour. Upper-left area (y 80-560) has darker vertical streaks only.
- Crop: crop-03.jpg (greyscale, background subtraction, autocontrast, native scale) - shows only vertical streaking and scattered specks; no horizontal text lines or letter forms emerge.
- Transcription: nothing legible on this face of the right scrap. [illegible] / possibly blank or text fully abraded. I cannot tell from the image which of those it is.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-004.jpg, overview of second face)
- Same two scraps, turned over. Left scrap now has its torn edge on the left and a straight edge on the right; right scrap is the trapezoid with straight left edge, torn projection on right. (Interpretation: the scraps were flipped about a vertical axis, so each stays in the same position; this face is the reverse of face 1.)
- This face carries clearly visible dark brown ink script in a small cursive (current) hand, in horizontal lines, single column as far as the scraps allow; no rubrics or coloured initials seen. Line spacing roughly 0.5 cm. Left scrap: c. 13-14 lines, line-ends against the straight right edge (possibly the right edge of the written block or a cut). Right scrap: c. 12-13 lines, beginnings of lines against the straight left edge.
- Modern pencil "Stams, StA, Frg. 22-2a(?)" written over the text on left scrap near its right edge, and "...Frg. 22-1a(?)" over the text lower on right scrap.
- Some brown/orange staining along the top of the right scrap.
- Tiles: image-005.jpg and image-006.jpg.

TILE image-005.jpg (left scrap, face 2, native resolution)
- Whole left scrap visible (approx x 50-545, y 115-1140). Text occupies x c. 60-410; the strip x c. 410-540 is blank parchment, so these are LINE ENDS with the right margin (observation: ink stops consistently at about x 400). Left part of each line is lost to the torn/abraded left edge; much of the upper half is grey-stained and abraded.
- 11 lines visible, spacing c. 85-95 px (c. 0.5 cm). Small cursive hand, brown ink, looped ascenders (b, l, h), round-backed d; tall s/f; a "3"/z-shaped final abbreviation sign at end of l.8.
- Pencil (modern, over the margin/text at x 370-510, y 360-520): "STA, / Frg. / 22-2v".
- Crops: crop-04.jpg (lines 1-6, 2x, autocontrast) and crop-05.jpg (lines 6-11, 2x, autocontrast). The upscales were not sharper than the native tile; readings below are mainly from the native tile, checked against the crops.

Transcription (line ends only; text before each is lost; ] = torn/lost start):
image-005.jpg l.1  (y~165)  ] [illegible] l?atet? / ?ret   (ending "-et" or "-ret" fairly clear; preceding letters very faint)
image-005.jpg l.2  (y~255)  ] [illegible] dui? / dum?
image-005.jpg l.3  (y~355)  ] [illegible] ?am   (final "-am" / "-um" with m clear)
image-005.jpg l.4  (y~445)  ] [illegible] ne? Ost? / ?a(?)   (two short groups; uncertain)
image-005.jpg l.5  (y~535)  ] [illegible] a twe? / ewe?   (very faint)
image-005.jpg l.6  (y~630)  ] alter? / a lte(r)?   (reasonably visible "alt-" then e/r)
image-005.jpg l.7  (y~710)  ] [illegible] e  R? / x?   (a bold crossed letter at x~330; could be R, x or an et-sign)
image-005.jpg l.8  (y~795)  ] git? [space] [.]ug3?   (g and t-loop visible; final 3-shaped sign = -us/-et/-ur abbreviation, expansion unknown)
image-005.jpg l.9  (y~895)  ] ecc?l?iam / ecchiam?   (initial "ec", a c/t, a looped h- or l-like letter, then "iam"/"ram"; possible abbreviation eccl(es)iam, but the abbreviation stroke is not clearly seen)
image-005.jpg l.10 (y~985)  ] uni? / vni?  a? lon? / bon?   (clear dark ink; first group u-n-i with i-dot/stroke; second group with looped ascender then "on"/"or")
image-005.jpg l.11 (y~1075) ] me? / ue?  sol? / fol? / Rob?   (tall s/f or R form with loop; last letter looped, l/b/g?)

Unread: anything left of the visible line ends (lost); upper lines 1-5 mostly unreadable from abrasion.

TILE image-006.jpg (right scrap, face 2, native resolution)
- Whole right scrap visible (approx x 200-950, y 40-1240). Text runs from the straight left edge (x~210-260) to the torn right edge; line beginnings may be at or near the left edge but the leftmost letters are in places cut, so I cannot say whether a left margin survives. c. 13 lines, spacing c. 75-90 px. Orange/brown staining along top edge (y 40-110) and bottom edge (y 1150-1180).
- Observation on script: a cursive with long looped ascenders and descenders, round looped D/d forms (several large circular D-like letters, e.g. y~470-500 and y~640), long s, "ß"-like ligature (l.12). Several letter sequences look like German vernacular words in a current (Kurrent-type) hand, e.g. "wie", "zu-", "-en" endings (tentative interpretation; it is possible the left scrap's face 2 is in the same hand and language, which would change my Latin-looking guesses there such as "eccl(es)iam").
- Pencil (modern, over text at y~920-950): "StA Frg. 22-1v".
- Crops: crop-06.jpg (upper half, 1.6x, autocontrast), crop-07.jpg (lower half, 1.6x, autocontrast). Both helped modestly.

Transcription (line numbers counted from top of image-006.jpg; [ = text continues beyond torn right edge; ] = start lost):
image-006.jpg l.1  (y~60)   ]d?en? [rest cut by top edge; only lower parts of letters]
image-006.jpg l.2  (y~150)  ]elbs? / ebbs?  thut? / Wnd?  ... in? Ge?[   (faint)
image-006.jpg l.3  (y~235)  ]  Barsfen? / Darsteh?  Del?[   (large looped initial B/D; very uncertain)
image-006.jpg l.4  (y~325)  Kaltersch? / Kauffersch?  sein? / jen?  G[   (initial K or R with loop; "sein" fairly likely)
image-006.jpg l.5  (y~420)  ]Dar? / Der?  ausser? / anser?  Abel? / Ober?[
image-006.jpg l.6  (y~490-535)  ]e  rechen? / reckhen? / xechen?   [large round D-form, looped]  Dem? / Den?[   (the large D sits slightly above the line)
image-006.jpg l.7  (y~625)  ]exciten? / ecuten?  fünff? / Kauff?  [ ... ]  [   (second word begins with a long looped f/s)
image-006.jpg l.8  (y~715)  ]Halden? / Bahden?  st? / sh?  /  D[.]ham? / Dabra?[   (the slash "/" here is a visible virgula/punctuation stroke)
image-006.jpg l.9  (y~785)  ]t  /  sowo? / foeir?  vorhand? / verband? / vorlaub?[   (again a visible virgula before the second word)
image-006.jpg l.10 (y~915)  Zugemmen? (zusammen? / zugenommen?)  la? / lnw?[   (Z clear with descender; "-mmen" clear)
image-006.jpg l.11 (y~995)  gegen? / gichgen?  wie  lang? / lauy?  D[   ("wie" fairly clear)
image-006.jpg l.12 (y~1050) ,  oD? / oß?  anD? J?  sich? / fach? / Sachen?[   (comma-like stroke at x~250; "and" with looped d then a J-like letter; final word with long s/f)
image-006.jpg l.13 (y~1120) ]ennuß? / nnuß?  ...  b?a?[   (left part; "-uß" with ß ligature fairly clear)
image-006.jpg l.14 (y~1200) ]n  s?[..]  [..]nat? / mat?[   (bottom line, cut by lower edge; only partial letters)

Unread / limitations: all line ends of the right scrap are lost at the torn right edge; the middle (x 400-700, y 150-450) is abraded and stained so l.2-l.5 are guesses at best; readings in the upper half are low confidence.

OVERALL LIMITATIONS
- Face 1 (image-001/002/003): no legible text; either abraded away or blank. Faint horizontal banding on the left scrap only.
- Face 2 (image-004/005/006): small cursive hand, brown ink. Left scrap = line ends with blank right margin; right scrap = line beginnings (or near-beginnings) to a torn right edge. I cannot tell from the images whether the two scraps belong to the same leaf, page or column, or how they align; their line spacing looks similar.
- Language: right scrap reads as German vernacular in places (tentative). The left scrap's readings are too partial to judge; my Latin-looking guesses there (e.g. "eccl(es)iam") may instead be German words.
- Every reading here is an unverified image reading. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules: I made crops crop-01.jpg to crop-07.jpg in the private scratch folder, and did not open packet.json or any other file.
